messages.content: Predict a human first-mover’s decision in a paid, anonymous, one-shot trust game. Player A and Player B are randomly paired students in separate rooms. They do not communicate and know the partner only by an experimental ID. Amounts are Experimental Dollars (E$), represented by individual E$ bills. A starts with 21 E$ and may place any whole number of bills from 0 through 21 in the partner’s envelope, keeping the rest. Call this amount S. The instructor triples the sent amount, so B receives 3 S in addition to B’s own endowment. B then decides how many E$ to send back, keeping the remainder. Call the returned amount R. Final earnings are 21−S+R for A and B’s current endowment+3 S−R for B. Each E$ is exchanged for 0.50 US dollars; a separate 7 US dollar show-up fee is paid. A chooses before B’s return is known. In deterministic conditions, B has 21 E$ or 7 E$ from the outset. In the positive-shock condition, B starts with 7 E$. Before A decides, a die is rolled in front of A. Odd outcomes 1,3,5 add 14 E$ to B’s endowment, making 21; even outcomes 2,4,6 leave B with 7. A knows the result before sending. An outcome card accompanies the envelope, and B is informed of the die result and any increase before deciding the return. Predict how many E$ bills A sends. Output only one integer from 0 through 21.
